identity_evidence.quote: This report presents a case of a 44-year-old female patient diagnosed with granulomatosis with polyangiitis five months ago

attribution_limitations: Rituximab start is described three ways: started at admission (case section), started as the patient recovered hemodynamic stability at one dose weekly for four weeks, and later resumed; the abstract places immunobiological therapy after the provisory pacemaker. The text does not say whether the two start statements are one start or two, so their order is left unknown.
The sentence reporting dehydration and absent respiratory, cardiac, infection, metabolic and electrolyte signs has no printed subject, and its time (admission or later) is not stated.
The anchor of "After six days" is not named in the sentence.

The abstract says corticosteroids and immunobiological therapy followed the provisory pacemaker, but the case section names only methylprednisolone before admission and no corticosteroid in the intensive care phase.
The Figure 3 caption names a Torsades de points rhythm while the text names multiple episodes of sustained ventricular tachycardia; the text does not equate them.

The pacemaker was turned off and withdrawn from use, while the case section says the patient is waiting for removal of the permanent pacemaker; the turned-off pacemaker is not explicitly identified as the permanent one.
The causal role of granulomatosis with polyangiitis in the heart block is hedged ("most likely cause"); the abstract and title word it as a conduction defect in a patient with the disease.
Table 1 day headings (Day 1, Day 3, Day 5, Day 19) have no named anchor; text statements that markers were normal or elevated carry no time and are not matched to table cells.
Leukogram and platelet units are printed "mil/mm" with comma-grouped values (10,900; 682,000).

Shock is named only in the discussion ("determination of shock diagnosis" by bedside echocardiography in this case); the case section reports bradycardia with hypotension and the abstract hemodynamic instability, but no shock diagnosis or type is stated there.

Negative infection and electrolyte findings are stated twice: in the admission paragraph and in the intensive care paragraph; they are kept as two items because the source places them at different points of the course.

claims.text: A 44-year-old female patient had granulomatosis with polyangiitis diagnosed five months earlier, with upper and lower respiratory tract involvement, positive c-ANCA, chronic unspecific inflammation on nasal mucosa biopsy and no renal involvement. Imaging showed bilateral lung nodules, sinus and ear changes, and CT of the skull and sinuses showed bilateral mastoiditis and pansinusitis. Cyclophosphamide and methylprednisolone gave an unsatisfactory response.
